summary: A consulting and technology-services company helping organisations build, change and operate systems, with cloud, AI and software-platform offerings.
description: Infosys combines delivery teams, consulting, engineering and platforms to solve customer technology and operating problems. A retail website project, bank-system change and continuing business-process service have different contracts and delivery needs.
money: Clients pay for services and relevant software or platform arrangements. Pricing, delivered work, employee and subcontractor costs, productivity, utilisation and currency influence earnings and collections.
customers: Organisations in financial services, manufacturing, retail, communications and other industries. The industries in the financial table describe customers, not businesses that Infosys owns.
drivers: Customer budgets, contract execution, service mix, pricing, people costs, automation, currency and collection of invoices.

groups.title: Consulting and application services
groups.examples: Application development, maintenance, enterprise systems and business consulting.
groups.explanation: Projects change a system; continuing support keeps it operating. Their revenue timing and responsibilities can differ.

groups.title: Cloud and infrastructure
groups.examples: Infosys Cobalt and related cloud, infrastructure and security work.
groups.explanation: Cloud transformation needs implementation and operation, not simply a software label.

groups.title: AI, data and experience
groups.examples: Infosys Topaz, analytics and the Aster marketing-services suite.
groups.explanation: These are sets of services, solutions and platforms; a brand name does not prove separately earned profit.

groups.title: Platforms and business processes
groups.examples: Finacle and other enterprise platforms, alongside business-process-management services.
groups.explanation: Licensing, implementation, support and process operation can involve different commercial arrangements.

basics.title: Services and customer sectors overlap
basics.text: A financial-services client can buy cloud, AI and application maintenance together. Do not add a service-market estimate to a reported industry segment as though it were another independent sale.

steps.title: Scope the business need
steps.text: Agree the problem, expected deliverables, contract basis and responsibility for outcomes.

steps.title: Organise delivery
steps.text: Match skills, tools and partner technology to the work while managing cost and quality.

steps.title: Perform and recognise revenue
steps.text: Deliver the service or contractual milestones under the relevant recognition policy.

steps.title: Bill, collect and expand
steps.text: Invoice, collect payments and compete for renewal or additional work.

specifics.title: Growth measures need a currency label
specifics.text: Dollar, rupee and constant-currency growth can differ. Constant currency adjusts the stated exchange-rate effect; it does not remove pricing or demand risk.

specifics.title: A deal needs time to become earnings
specifics.text: Contract value can include renewals and work over future periods. Margin depends on staffing, transition costs, automation and actual scope delivered.

specifics.title: AI adoption needs a commercial test
specifics.text: Productivity improvements may lower delivery effort, while clients may ask for lower prices or different outcomes. Paid demand and realised economics matter more than an offering’s name.

watch: Are deal wins creating realised growth?
Contract size and current delivery are different.

Read large-deal commentary with revenue, ramp-up timing and renewals. Identify what is new scope versus replacement of an existing contract; do not equate pipeline or total contract value with annual sales.
Financial services and retail can face different cycles.
Compare industry-segment commentary and results using the same period. A slowdown in a major sector can matter more than rapid growth from a small base elsewhere.
What is behind the operating margin?
Pricing and delivery efficiency interact with staff costs.
Read utilisation definitions, attrition, wage changes, subcontracting and onsite/offshore mix alongside achieved margin. Distinguish reported segment operating income from consolidated net profit.
Are billed and unbilled balances collected?
Accounting revenue can precede customer cash.

Review trade receivables, unbilled revenue, operating cash flow and contract terms. Explain a balance change in relation to sales and billing schedules rather than judging it from its absolute size alone.
Is transformation demand improving client economics?
Cloud and AI spending must solve a real problem.
Look for implemented customer work and the stated scope of AI or cloud revenue. Separate management’s forecasts and addressable-market estimates from completed, paid delivery.
risks: Customers may delay decisions, reduce scope or negotiate lower prices.
Wages, reskilling, attrition or an unfavourable delivery mix can reduce earnings.
Complex transformations can run late or expose systems and information, creating costs and reputational damage.
Exchange rates, immigration and data rules and new automation models can change demand and delivery economics.
context: A platform and a service team can solve one client problem

A banking platform may require configuration, migration and continuing support. Understand which activities are contracted and billed rather than treating the software name as a standalone earnings engine.
quiz: Does constant-currency growth show that profits grew at the same rate?
No. It adjusts a currency effect on the stated revenue measure. Staff costs, pricing, mix and other expenses still affect profit.

financialNotes.title: The table groups customers, not platforms
financialNotes.text: The verified segment rows cover industries such as Financial Services and Retail. Their segment operating income must be reconciled to company profit; it is not a disclosed profit for Cobalt, Topaz or Finacle.

financialNotes.title: Read cash separately
financialNotes.text: An industry with high segment operating income can still have billing or collection timing differences. Continue with the consolidated cash-flow statement and customer balances before concluding how much cash was generated.
